content: Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes, as it can prolong the QTc interval and increase the risk of serious arrhythmias, including Torsades de Pointes and sudden death. Close monitoring is recommended in such cases. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of vorinostat by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of ziprasidone by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. Crizotinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but caution is advised. Adagrasib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsades de Pointes and other serious arrhythmias. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, frequent ECG monitoring is recommended. Albuterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Alfuzosin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Aluminum hydroxide decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Amiodarone toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Amisulpride and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administration is unavoidable. Amitriptyline toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Amoxapine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Anagrelide and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Apomorphine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Arformoterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Aripiprazole and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Arsenic trioxide toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Artemether and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Artemether/lumefantrine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Asenapine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Asenapine transdermal and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Atazanavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Rilpivirine is not expected to affect the plasma concentrations of co-administered protease inhibitors. Atidarsagene autotemcel and rilpivirine should not be co-administered. Antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. ARTs should be discontinued at least 1 month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Atomoxetine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Azithromycin toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Bedaquiline and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Betibeglogene autotemcel and rilpivirine should not be co-administered. ARTs should be discontinued at least 1 month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Buprenorphine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Buprenorphine buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection forms all prolong the QTc interval when co-administered with rilpivirine. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Calcium acetate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Calcium carbonate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, and calcium/vitamin D all decrease rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Antacids should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Carbamazepine decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in a loss of virologic response and resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. Ceritinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Chlorpromazine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Cimetidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. H2 antagonists should be administered at least 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. Ciprofloxacin toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Citalopram toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clarithromycin increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine also increases clarithromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clomipramine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Clozapine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. Conivaptan increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Cyclobenzaprine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Dasatinib toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Degarelix toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Desflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be used. Desipramine toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. Deutetrabenazine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. Dexamethasone decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in a loss of virologic response and resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. Dexlansoprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in treatment failure and resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. Didanosine and rilpivirine interact due to effects on CYP3A4 metabolism. Didanosine should be administered on an empty stomach at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine, which should be taken with a meal. No dose adjustment is required, but close monitoring is recommended. Disopyramide toxicity is increased by rilpivirine due to QTc interval prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised.
